title: When a sketch becomes a world

segments.headline: A line is a beginning
segments.narration: What if a sketch could become something we can walk around? Here, the original Ryo avatar stands inside today’s iPad scan. A simple orbital laboratory begins with a pen and three circles.

segments.headline: Keep the original marks
segments.narration: Watch the tip. Each line appears exactly where the pen travels. These are persistent curves, not pictures waiting to be replaced. The same points will carry the idea into space.

segments.headline: Let the drawing acquire depth
segments.narration: Now the drawing opens. Its circles tilt, widen, and become three dimensional orbits. Nothing cuts to a new diagram. The original curves continuously change shape, and moving planets give them behavior.

segments.headline: Reach into the representation
segments.narration: Ryo steps beside the model and reaches for the middle orbit. Tilting its plane changes the path that the planet actually follows. The representation is also a control surface: the change stays in the world.

segments.headline: Make time a material
segments.narration: Now speed up time. The planets travel faster around their existing paths. The camera moves with us, revealing the depth that a flat explanation would hide. This is an illustrative orbital model, not a scale model of our solar system.

segments.headline: From watching to exploring
segments.narration: The portable demo lets you change inclination, time speed, and the transition between sketch and space. Inspired by Chalktalk and dynamic media, it makes a small idea executable. The film is authored choreography, not live sketch recognition. The controls are real.
